content: REPS2, also known as RalBP1-associated Eps domain-containing protein 2, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the REPS2 gene. The protein product of the REPS2 gene is a component of a protein complex that plays a regulatory role in the endocytosis of growth factor receptors. This protein directly interacts with a GTPase-activating protein that operates downstream of the small G protein Ral. The expression of REPS2 can negatively influence receptor internalization and inhibit signaling pathways mediated by growth factors. Additionally, multiple transcript variants of the REPS2 gene have been identified, which encode different isoforms of the protein. REPS2 has been demonstrated to interact with several other proteins, including EPN1 (Epsin 1), EPS15 (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Pathway Substrate 15), and RALBP1 (Ral-binding protein 1).
